title: Project Coordinator
description: This position may work remotely from any of the following US states: AZ, CA, CO, DC, FL, GA, IL, MD, MA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA. Additionally, the position may work remotely from any of the following countries outside of the US: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Canada, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, South Africa, and Zambia. Hiring range for a US-based candidate is $65,000 to $85,000 annually. Compensation for this position will be determined on the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Reporting to the CEO, the Project Coordinator provides support to the Senior Leadership Team. Responsibilities supporting Ipas’s President & CEO include but are not limited to, scheduling, expense reporting, and support with board of directors’ meetings. In addition, the Project Coordinator will provide project support to the CFO and COO. This position is a combination of administrative and project support for a range of activities that will likely change depending on the needs of the organization. Therefore, the incumbent must be flexible, knowledgeable of Ipas systems and processes, and be able to manage multiple needs and urgent priorities while maintaining confidentiality. Summary of Responsibilities Administrative Support Provides broad administrative support, including scheduling and coordinating meetings, and travel planning for the Ipas-US Senior Leadership Team (CEO, CFO, COO) . Coordinates relevant meetings and preparations to include calendar invites, agenda, room set up (virtual or in-person), interpretation, and technology needs, including electronic conferencing tools. Supports budget development, monitoring, and expense processing, and tracks spending for activities for the Office of the President. Supports administrative and financial tasks for the US SLT team. Coordinates domestic and international travel arrangements for senior staff and board members, and Board meeting hotel and event needs (meals, meeting space, transportation, etc.) Coordinate State registration and support the CFO and CEO with completing annual applications. Maintains the US SLT team’s SharePoint site (Luna) and organizes electronic document storage. Project Responsibilities Summarizes, prioritizes, and researches information into a concise and usable format for the SLT to review Creates or directs creation of reports, budgets, and contract processing materials for SLT Coordinates high level projects and responds to or routes priority or confidential inquiries from external or internal sources with correspondence or other messaging on behalf of the SLT. Minimum Requirements Bachelor’s degree in related field. 5-7 years of relevant work experience in planning, administration support and logistics 2-3 years of project support experience including support for budgeting, expense management and financial procedures. Ability to process multiple priorities from multiple senior leaders timely and effectively Effective cultural awareness as indicated by the ability to work in a diverse and dynamic environment with people from diverse backgrounds Strong technical expertise in Zoom, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Outlook, and calendar management Strong working knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English Attention to detail, quality, and ability to follow-up and follow-through Ability to work both independently and collaboratively, as needed Ability to work autonomously with general direction, clear targets, and limited supervision. Ability to professionally and confidentially interface with all levels of the organization and leadership Ability to have a flexible schedule to accommodate senior leaders in different time zones Commitment to reproductive justice Ability to travel up to 10% Preferred Qualifications Certification in Project Management Experience managing grants, funds, and/or budgets. Anticipates and responds to needs of each member of SLT Ability to coordinate with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities while being sensitive to time and budget constraints. Fluency in other languages (Spanish, French, Portuguese or others) Working environment Remote work; travel up to 10% Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. title: Senior Medical Scientist
description: This position is remote-based. Salary range for US-based candidate is $165,000.00 to $180,000.00. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Position may work remotely from any of the following US states: AZ, CA, CO, DC, FL, GA, MD, MA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA. Additionally, the position may work remotely from any of the following countries outside of the US: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Canada, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. The Senior Medical Scientist will provide technical leadership to help ensure that the best available evidence supports quality and continuous improvement in safe abortion, contraception, and gender-based violence management across development and humanitarian contexts. This role will strengthen abortion availability, accessibility, acceptability and quality through formal health systems and self-care pathways by establishing and enhancing global technical tools, standards, processes, monitoring mechanisms, and partnerships that contribute to a sustainable abortion ecosystem. Summary of Responsibilities The Senior Medical Scientist is a subject matter expert, using clinical expertise, evolving evidence and strategic partnerships to advance Ipas’s mission at the global level. In collaboration with key staff across the organization, Senior Medical Scientist will advance innovative initiatives and provide strategic guidance and technical assistance on safe abortion, contraception and GBV care quality and access. The Senior Medical Scientist disseminates new evidence through publications and presentations; conducts training; represents Ipas externally, advocating for the organization’s mission within the broader reproductive health field; and builds partnerships with colleague organizations to maximize impact. Organizational Leadership and Strategy: Provides technical leadership to develop and test innovative approaches to improve quality abortion and contraception care (e.g., global quality indicators, quality improvement processes) and to integrate safe abortion and postabortion contraception into SRHR programming for Ipas support programs and in emergency crisis settings Program, technical, or functional content of the job: Provide and/or analyze evidence based technical content used for advocacy opportunities related to safe abortion for Ipas supported programs and external coalitions Develop technical tools and resources translating evidence based clinical updates into health services Provides technical leadership on quality and regulatory processes pertinent to the Ipas MVA product line, as well as infection prevention and MVA processing Supports training of Ipas supported sites and partners on content such as VCAT, clinical management of abortion and contraception care, trauma-informed care, legal risk assessment, etc. Leads and/or significant participation in clinical/technical research and technical evidence dissemination for abortion/contraception clinical practice improvement Prepare and/or analyze service delivery data and issue clinical recommendations for continuous improvement of quality of care across the pathways to care. Resource mobilization: Supports fundraising initiatives by contributing to donor proposals and preparation/review of donor reports Communications & representation: Write periodic evidence summaries for internal communications with technical staff across the network Provides external leadership, Ipas representation, and advocacy as required at national, regional and international conferences and events Disseminates evidence externally through presentations and publications Position Requirements A deep commitment to sexual and reproductive health and rights, especially abortion, contraception and GBV care access Demonstrated contribution to the development of technical tools, standards, guidelines, and SRHR research. Professional-level fluency in English (speaking, reading, and writing) Proven ability to support and strengthen the capacity of teams, including through training, supportive supervision, strong communication, nonhierarchical leadership approaches, and modeling the Ipas core values. Demonstrated capacity and commitment to good stewardship of funds, including strong skills in work planning, budgeting, financial monitoring, and data-driven problem solving. Proven ability to build positive working relationships in a multicultural and complex implementation contexts with diverse internal teams and external partners Education Advanced clinical degree (e.g nursing, midwifery) Experience 10 years’ experience in clinical practice including reproductive health care and experience applying scientific clinical information to practical training and programs Substantive experience with evaluation of quality in clinical care and quality improvement. Substantive knowledge and experience of international reproductive health programs and systems in low-resource and humanitarian settings Knowledge of key partners and influencers in our field Experience working in multicultural teams Preferred Qualifications PhD or DrPH and/or significant experience in research Strong clinical background Experience working in humanitarian contexts and/or working with humanitarian implementing agencies Established relationships with non-profit organizations and advocacy groups Proficiency with at least one Ipas working language, such as French, Portuguese, or Spanish. Strong preference for advanced practice midwife or nurse Working environment: Ability to travel up to 20% of the time internationally, including in crisis settings Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. title: Global Audience Insight & Engagement Advisor
description: This position is remote-based. Salary range for US-based candidate is $65,000.00 to $72,000.00. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country and the applicable statutory laws, in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Position may work remotely from any of the following US states: AZ, CA, CO, DC, FL, GA, MD, MA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA. Additionally, the position may work remotely from any of the following countries outside of the US: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Canada, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. The Audience Insights and Engagement Advisor is responsible for using audience insights, measurement, and performance data to strengthen engagement across Ipas’s communications channels, including digital platforms, email, campaigns, publications, events, and other audience-facing initiatives. S/he tracks audience needs, behaviors, and responses; analyzes content and campaign performance; and translates findings into clear recommendations that improve reach, relevance, engagement, and impact. This role helps create, disseminate, monitor, and optimize compelling content and communications approaches based on what priority audiences need, value, and respond to. Working closely with Communications, Development, country teams, and other colleagues, the Advisor helps design audience-informed strategies/tactics and campaigns with measurable objectives, evaluates results, and makes data-informed adjustments that raise awareness, deepen supporter engagement, and support organizational goals. This individual plays a key role in shaping engagement strategies grounded in audience understanding, consistent measurement, and alignment with broader organizational priorities. Primary Responsibilities: Develop and execute audience engagement strategies grounded in audience insights, channel performance, and clear communications goals, coordinating with Communications colleagues to ensure alignment with the overall editorial calendar and organizational priorities. Track and interpret audience behavior, feedback, and engagement across communications channels, including social media, email, web, publications, campaigns, events, and other audience-facing initiatives. Design and maintain reporting systems that measure reach, engagement, conversion, audience growth, message resonance, and campaign effectiveness, translating data into practical recommendations for decision-making. Exercise decision-making authority for routine audience engagement, channel optimization, and performance reporting decisions within approved communications strategies and budgets. Guide country teams in developing audience-informed communications approaches that reflect the Ipas brand and use audience and performance data to inform strategy, message development, and channel choices. Collaborate with Communications and fundraising teams to design campaigns with precise objectives, defined audiences, measurable outcomes, and clear learning and reporting plans. Implement and optimize engagement approaches across paid, earned, shared, and owned channels to distribute content, strengthen relationships, grow priority audiences, and support individual donor engagement. Actively engage with followers, supporters, partners, and stakeholders across platforms Collaborate with the Content Manager, Audience Engagement Specialist, and other colleagues on audience segmentation, message testing, and performance metrics to inform campaign design and content creation. Monitor emerging trends, technologies, audience behaviors, communications practices, and relevant regulations, assessing implications for engagement, measurement, and content strategy. Manage campaign logistics, ensuring adherence to timelines, budgets, reporting expectations, and effective communication with all stakeholders. Present clear, actionable metrics for the CEO Dashboard and other reporting needs, showing the reach, engagement, audience growth, message resonance, and impact of Communications initiatives. Contribute to building the communications and brand ambassadorship capacity of the Ipas network by helping gather feedback on staff needs, sharing audience and performance insights, offering technical assistance as requested, and supporting education, skills-building, and knowledge-sharing activities organized by the Network Communications service node. Performance KPIs: Audience growth and engagement: Demonstrates measurable improvement in priority audience reach, engagement rate, follower or subscriber growth, and meaningful interaction across social, email, web, campaign, event, and publication channels. Insight quality and application: Produces clear audience insights, segmentation findings, test results, and performance analyses that are regularly used to shape content, campaigns, channel choices, and engagement strategies. Campaign performance: Supports campaigns with defined objectives, audiences, timelines, and measurement plans; tracks results such as reach, click-through rate, conversion, content engagement, message resonance, and learning outcomes. Reporting and decision support: Delivers timely, accurate, and actionable reports for the CEO Dashboard and other internal needs, highlighting what is working, what is changing, and what adjustments are recommended. Cross-team collaboration: Builds effective working relationships with Communications, Development, country teams, and other colleagues, ensuring audience insights and performance data are incorporated into shared plans and products. Optimization and learning: Identifies trends, tests new approaches, documents lessons learned and recommends practical improvements that increase communications effectiveness over time. Minimum Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, digital technology or related field Five years of experience in social/digital marketing and strategic communications in media, non- profit, or agency environment Familiarity with social justice and human rights causes and initiatives Fluency in multiple social media platform management tools and trends Excellent grasp of social media, web and email metrics and best practices (Sprout, Google Analytics, etc.) ExperiencewithMicrosoft OfficeSuite Preferred: Some non-English language fluency Experience in a global nonprofit Graphic design experience Competencies: Proven track record as a collaborative team player who listens, contributes and enjoys teamwork Knowledge of reproductive justice and health messaging Innovative thinker Ipas is strongly committed to providing a work environment that is free from all forms of harassment, discrimination, and inequity. title: Strategic Partnership Manager - Africa
description: This is a remote position. Compensation for this position will be determined by the prevailing market rate in the employee's country in addition to Ipas's own pay philosophy and other factors, such as the employee's experience level and expertise. Candidates based in the following countries are eligible to apply: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Kenya/Alliance locations, Malawi, Mozambique, Nigeria, South Africa, Zambia. Ipas seeks a Strategic Partnership Manager to strengthen resource mobilization and the partnership portfolio in Africa. The manager will identify, cultivate, and expand a pipeline of institutional donors, foundations, corporate partners, and strategic collaborators whose priorities align with Ipas's mission and values. The role will provide targeted business development support for high-value funding opportunities, deepen engagement with priority donors and partners, and contribute to compelling donor-facing materials, including expressions of interest, concept notes, proposals, budgets, presentations, results frameworks, and partnership strategies. The Strategic Partnership Manager will demonstrate a strong commitment to reproductive justice, including human rights, abortion rights, gender equity, diversity, equity, and inclusion. The role will collaborate across the Ipas Network and promote shared leadership, trust, and inclusive, non-hierarchical approaches to learning and collaboration, while supporting effective stewardship of donor resources and adherence to Ipas's mission, values, and standards. Primary Responsibilities: 1. Opportunity Pipeline Development and Donor/Partner Intelligence Map priority foundations, institutional funders, corporate partners, and strategic implementing partners aligned with Ipass mission and work. Analyze funder priorities, eligibility, timelines, typical award size, indirect cost expectations, compliance considerations, and relationship pathways. Identify and track requests for proposals, calls for proposals, invitations, and relationship-led opportunities, and maintain an up-to-date pipeline tracker. Support go/no-go decisions through fit assessments, competitiveness analysis, and risk and feasibility review, including deadlines, staffing, partnership needs, cost share, and indirect rate constraints. 2. External Relations and Resource Mobilization Support Develop donor and partner engagement plans for priority prospects, including objectives, messages, decision-makers, and follow-up actions. Draft and refine positioning materials, including capability statements, one-pagers, brief slide decks, project summaries, and boilerplate language. Build Ipas Network intelligence on key trends and opportunities in Africa. Work with the Communications Service Node to contribute to external communications through the Ipas website, newsletters, and social media. Prepare talking points, briefing notes, and agendas for external meetings; when requested, participate in meetings, capture next steps, and support follow-up. Advise on partnership strategy, including lead versus sub-award roles, consortium roles, negotiation points, partner mapping, and outreach. Work with the Development Service Node to report quarterly and annually on fundraising efforts and results and participate in annual management cycle activities. 3. Proposal Development, Review, and Quality Assurance Support donor-facing submissions, including expressions of interest, concept notes, and full proposals, in coordination with internal teams and partners. Develop and review technical narratives for compliance, clarity, and responsiveness to donor evaluation criteria. Support required annexes, including results frameworks or log frames, workplans, monitoring, evaluation and learning plans, risk matrices, and staffing plans. Coordinate with finance counterparts to develop and quality-check budgets and budget narratives for alignment with the technical approach and donor cost rules. Provide structured written feedback through tracked comments or review memos and participate in review meetings to agree on revisions and next steps. Minimum Requirements: Ten or more years’ work experience managing programs and projects with increasing complexity and responsibility Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field Demonstrated experience in business development, fundraising, and/or proposal development for NGOs, social enterprises, or mission-driven organizations. Strong understanding of institutional donor environments, including bilateral and multilateral agencies, foundations, and partnership or consortium approaches. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and French. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, coordinate across teams, and deliver high-quality products with minimal supervision. Proven record of developing competitive proposals and donor-facing products, including complex budgets and results frameworks or log frames. Subject-matter expertise in sexual and reproductive health and rights and reproductive justice, and/or experience working internationally. Deep commitment to reproductive justice, human rights, abortion rights, gender equity, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Commitment to shared leadership, trust, and inclusive, non-hierarchical ways of working. Travel & Work Environment Regular travel within Africa and to strategic hubs, in accordance with Ipas travel policies. Virtual collaboration with colleagues across the Ipas Network and across time zones. Weekly written progress updates and biweekly virtual check-ins with the Director of Development and relevant staff. Deliverables submitted electronically in editable formats, such as Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, unless otherwise agreed. title: Workday Financial System Administrator (Remote)
description: This position is remote-based. Salary for US-based candidate is $120,000.00. Position may work remotely from any of the following US states: AZ, CA, CO, DC, FL, GA, MD, MA, MI, NJ, NY, NC, PA, SC, TX, VA, WA. Additionally, the position may work remotely from any of the following countries outside of the US: Bangladesh, Bolivia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Cote d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Malawi, Mexico, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nepal, Nigeria, South Africa, and Zambia. The Workday Finance System Administrator (Sys Admin) provides routine support for the following Workday functional areas: Procurement and Suppliers, Expense Management, Banking and Settlement, Financial Accounting (General Ledger and Reporting), Business Assets, Projects, Budgeting and Financial Planning. Ipas utilizes Workday’s full suite of solutions for Human Capital Management (HCM) and Financial Management, and this role will collaborate closely with their counterpart in HR to ensure data integrity across functional areas. • This role will directly manage and maintain the Workday system. This role will perform Workday administrative functions including security maintenance, business process configuration, tenant configuration, data loads, integrations, and upgrades. This person will be responsible for engaging short-term consultants, as needed, for the success of projects. The Workday System Administrator understands and is familiar with the processes performed by functional Finance business areas. The role coordinates and seeks alignment across business units to maximize efficiency and productivity, and identifies and addresses areas for process improvement and operational efficiencies. The Workday System Administrator is a skilled communicator, a strong documenter of processes and decisions, and is able to clearly and effectively provide updates on the status of ongoing projects, issues, and upcoming needs. Primary Responsibilities Provides routine support for the following Workday functional areas: Procurement and Suppliers, Expense Management, Banking and Settlement, Financial Accounting (General Ledger and Reporting), Business Assets, Projects, Budgeting and Financial Planning. Supports these functional areas in a production environment and works independently with minimal oversight. Performs Workday administrative functions including security maintenance, business process configuration, tenant configuration, data loads, integrations, and upgrades. Monitors tickets and responds to daily support requests and resolves issues. Proactively communicates with internal customers. Provides technical and functional expertise including solution review, alternative options for resolution, and recommendations. Creates technical configuration including business process workflow, custom fields, custom validations, custom reports, dashboards, integrations, and access rights. Write standard, advanced, matrix and composite reports as well as creating complex calculated fields, custom objects, and worksheets. Proactively validates and identifies technical/functional issues, recommends solutions, and drives timely decisions. Acts as the organization’s lead change agent in preparation and implementation of new system rollouts and upgrades. Independently implements enhancements and solutions for identified issues including reporting and integrations, while also identifying skills needed from external resources to fill internal knowledge gaps and managing these resources. Monitors system performance, efficiency, and use. Develops triage criteria for assigning tickets among subject matter experts. Facilitates cross-functional team meetings. Liaise with Workday user community to access best practices. Other duties as assigned. Requirements Minimum Bachelor’s degree in related field. 5 or more years relevant experience. At least 3 years Workday ERP experience, with expertise in FDM and exposure to HRIS. Experience managing contractors, and vendors. Expertise in the design, implementation, and deployment of user-centric systems, with a focus on usability. Proven record of clear communication (oral and written) with diverse audiences and a record of producing clear documentation. Preferred Skills Workday ERP certifications in Financials, and/or Report Writing. Experience with Adaptive Planning and Workday Grants and Awards. Rich skills and experience with Microsoft solutions especially Excel, PowerPoint. Experience with global systems deployment. Experience with Six Sigma, Agile, and/or other methodologies. Expertise in collaborative technologies including Microsoft solutions (SharePoint, OneDrive, Planner, etc.) and/or other project management tools. Strong understanding of systems development life cycle (SDLC) and ITIL framework and principals. International non-profit/NGO experience.
